title: Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement Dashboards
brief: Wire the 5 mock-data Lean pages (KaizenBoard, ValueStream, KanbanBoard, RootCause, A3Report) to real backend engines, add three new executive-grade pages (ExecutiveDashboard, ShopFloorTV, DailyFlashReport), and enhance the already-wired OEEDashboardPage with Six Big Losses breakdown, 30-day rolling trends, and machine drill-down. All pages depend on pause_periods and scrap data from BIZ-MS0 and real-time tracking from BIZ-MS1.

phases.title: Wire Existing Lean Pages to Real Backend
phases.description: Replace all hardcoded seed arrays in the five mock-data Lean pages with real API calls. KaizenBoard pulls improvement_notes from TimeClockEngine. ValueStream pulls routing steps from JobLifecycleEngine. KanbanBoard pulls dispatch queues from MachineDispatchEngine. RootCause pulls scrap incidents from TimeClockEngine and wires to TroubleshootingEngine. A3Report auto-populates from OEE + scrap + Kaizen data and generates PDFs.

units.title: Wire KaizenBoardPage to real improvement notes data

steps.instruction: Read web/src/pages/KaizenBoardPage.tsx in full (523 lines). Identify every reference to SEED_SUGGESTIONS, SEED_PROJECTS, and SEED_CONTRIBUTORS. List each hardcoded array and any synthetic state initialization before proceeding.

Add three API functions to web/src/api/client.ts: (a) kaizenSuggestions(params?: { status?: string; employeeId?: string; dateFrom?: string; dateTo?: string }) — calls GET /api/v1/erp/kaizen-suggestions with query params, returns KaizenSuggestion[]; (b) kaizenScore(suggestionId: string, score: { impact: number; effort: number; estimatedSavings: number; scoredBy: string }) — calls POST /api/v1/erp/kaizen-score with body; (c) kaizenUpdateStatus(suggestionId: string, status: 'submitted' | 'reviewing' | 'implemented' | 'deferred', updatedBy: string, notes?: string) — calls POST /api/v1/erp/kaizen-status with body.

In KaizenBoardPage.tsx, replace the SEED_SUGGESTIONS initialization: remove the hardcoded array and replace with a useEffect that calls kaizenSuggestions() on mount and stores results in state. Add loading and error states. Show a spinner while loading and an error banner on failure.

Replace SEED_CONTRIBUTORS with a derived calculation: compute contributors from the live suggestions list by grouping suggestion.submitted_by, counting suggestions_submitted and suggestions_implemented per contributor, then sort descending by suggestions_implemented first, then suggestions_submitted. Do NOT call a separate API for this — derive from the already-fetched suggestions array.

Replace SEED_PROJECTS (before/after tracker) with suggestions whose status === 'implemented' and that have a before_condition and after_condition field. Wire the 'Mark Implemented' flow to call kaizenUpdateStatus(id, 'implemented', ...) and then re-fetch the suggestions list.

Wire the impact scoring form: when a lead or hr_manager clicks 'Score', open a modal with inputs for impact (1-10), effort (1-5), and estimatedSavings (dollar field). On submit, call kaizenScore(suggestionId, { impact, effort, estimatedSavings, scoredBy: currentUser.id }). Reload the suggestion from the API response to update the card in place.

Add GET /api/v1/erp/kaizen-suggestions route to src/routes/erp.ts: query TimeClockEngine for all job_time_entries where improvement_note IS NOT NULL and IS NOT EMPTY. Map each entry to KaizenSuggestion shape: { id, submitted_by: employee_name, submitted_at: stop_time, improvement_note, job_number, status: 'submitted', impact_score, effort_score, estimated_savings, before_condition, after_condition }. Suggestions are stored in a kaizen_suggestions table (see migration step). Require verifyToken middleware.

Add POST /api/v1/erp/kaizen-score and POST /api/v1/erp/kaizen-status routes to src/routes/erp.ts. Both require verifyToken and requireRole('lead'). kaizen-score updates the row in kaizen_suggestions table. kaizen-status updates the status column and appends a status_notes entry. Return the updated suggestion.

Create migration src/db/migrations/014-kaizen-suggestions.sql: CREATE TABLE kaizen_suggestions (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, job_time_entry_id INTEGER REFERENCES job_time_entries(id), submitted_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, improvement_note TEXT NOT NULL, job_number VARCHAR(50), status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'submitted' CHECK (status IN ('submitted', 'reviewing', 'implemented', 'deferred')), impact_score INTEGER CHECK (impact_score BETWEEN 1 AND 10), effort_score INTEGER CHECK (effort_score BETWEEN 1 AND 5), estimated_savings NUMERIC(10,2), scored_by VARCHAR(100), scored_at TIMESTAMPTZ, before_condition TEXT, after_condition TEXT, status_notes JSONB DEFAULT '[]', created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()); CREATE INDEX idx_kaizen_status ON kaizen_suggestions(status); CREATE INDEX idx_kaizen_submitted_by ON kaizen_suggestions(submitted_by);
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors. Verify no references to SEED_SUGGESTIONS, SEED_PROJECTS, or SEED_CONTRIBUTORS remain in KaizenBoardPage.tsx.

deliverables.description: All three seed arrays replaced with real API calls. Suggestions load from /api/v1/erp/kaizen-suggestions. Scoring calls kaizenScore(). Status transitions call kaizenUpdateStatus(). Contributors derived from live data.
kaizenSuggestions(), kaizenScore(), kaizenUpdateStatus() API methods added.
GET /api/v1/erp/kaizen-suggestions, POST /api/v1/erp/kaizen-score, POST /api/v1/erp/kaizen-status routes added with auth.
kaizen_suggestions table with status check constraint, indexes on status and submitted_by.

exit_conditions: No references to SEED_SUGGESTIONS, SEED_PROJECTS, or SEED_CONTRIBUTORS remain in KaizenBoardPage.tsx
Kaizen board loads real improvement_notes from TimeClockEngine job entries
Impact scoring modal saves impact, effort, estimatedSavings to database via API
Status transitions (reviewing/implemented/deferred) persist and reload the card
Top contributors list is derived from live suggestion data — no hardcoded contributor array
Before/after tracker shows only suggestions with status='implemented'
All three API routes require auth token — unauthenticated requests return 401
npm run build:fast passes with 0 errors
abort_criteria: TimeClockEngine.getJobTimeEntries() does not return improvement_note field — field was not added in BIZ-MS0
BIZ-MS0 migration 012-job-time-enhancements.sql was not applied — improvement_note column missing from job_time_entries table
units.rollback: Restore SEED_SUGGESTIONS, SEED_PROJECTS, SEED_CONTRIBUTORS arrays in KaizenBoardPage.tsx from git; remove kaizenSuggestions, kaizenScore, kaizenUpdateStatus from client.ts; remove the three API routes from erp.ts; rollback migration 014.

units.title: Wire ValueStreamPage to real job lifecycle routing data

steps.instruction: Read web/src/pages/ValueStreamPage.tsx in full (410 lines). Identify every reference to PROCESS_STEPS, METRIC_TILES, and WASTES. Note how process boxes are rendered — SVG, CSS, or a library — before proceeding.

Add getValueStream(jobId: string) to web/src/api/client.ts — calls GET /api/v1/erp/value-stream/:jobId. Returns ValueStreamData shape: { job_number, customer, order_created_at, first_part_shipped_at, total_lead_time_sec, process_steps: Array<{ step_name, operation_code, sequence, estimated_cycle_time_sec, actual_cycle_time_sec, wait_time_sec, wip_count, operator_count, machine_id, is_value_added }>, takt_time_sec, value_added_ratio, cycle_efficiency_pct }.

In ValueStreamPage.tsx, add a job number search bar at the top. When the user enters a job number and submits, call getValueStream(jobId) and store the result in state. Replace PROCESS_STEPS with the live process_steps array from the API response. Replace METRIC_TILES with derived values: Lead Time from total_lead_time_sec, Takt Time from takt_time_sec, Value-Added Ratio from value_added_ratio, Cycle Efficiency from cycle_efficiency_pct.

Replace WASTES (static waste categories) with a computed waste summary derived from the process_steps array: aggregate wait_time_sec per step, identify steps where actual_cycle_time_sec > estimated_cycle_time_sec * 1.2 (overrun), count WIP triangles from wip_count. Group into waste categories: Waiting (sum of wait_time_sec), Overprocessing (steps where actual > estimated * 1.2), Inventory (sum of wip_count across all steps). Render these as the waste panel.

Add GET /api/v1/erp/value-stream/:jobId route to src/routes/erp.ts. Require verifyToken. Call JobLifecycleEngine.getJob(jobId) to get the job. Then for each routing step in job.routing_steps, query job_time_entries where job_number = jobId AND operation_code = step.operation_code to compute actual_cycle_time_sec (sum of hours_worked * 3600 for production entries). Compute wait_time_sec as time_gap between consecutive step start times. Compute value_added_ratio as (sum of actual_cycle_time for is_value_added=true steps) / total_lead_time_sec. Return the full ValueStreamData shape.
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors. Verify no references to PROCESS_STEPS, METRIC_TILES, or WASTES remain in ValueStreamPage.tsx.

deliverables.description: All three seed arrays replaced. Job search bar drives API call. Process boxes show actual vs estimated cycle time per operation. WIP triangles from wip_count. Lead time and VA ratio from real timestamps.
getValueStream(jobId) API method added.
GET /api/v1/erp/value-stream/:jobId route added, wired to JobLifecycleEngine and job_time_entries.

exit_conditions: No references to PROCESS_STEPS, METRIC_TILES, or WASTES remain in ValueStreamPage.tsx

Process boxes show actual vs estimated cycle time — overruns highlighted in yellow/red
WIP triangles rendered from active/paused job counts per operation from wip_count field
Lead time tile shows order_created_at to first_part_shipped_at in hours

Takt time overlay sourced from takt_time_sec in job routing
API route requires auth token
npm run build:fast passes with 0 errors
abort_criteria: JobLifecycleEngine does not expose routing_steps on the job object — wiring would require structural changes outside this milestone scope
job_time_entries table does not have operation_code column — BIZ-MS0 model enhancement was not applied

units.title: Wire KanbanBoardPage to real dispatch queue data

steps.instruction: Read web/src/pages/KanbanBoardPage.tsx in full (507 lines). Identify every reference to INITIAL_COLUMNS, INITIAL_JOBS, and HEIJUNKA_DATA. Note the drag-and-drop library in use (likely react-dnd or dnd-kit) and the column ID structure before proceeding.

Add three API functions to web/src/api/client.ts: (a) getDispatchBoard(departmentId?: string) — calls GET /api/v1/erp/dispatch-board with optional dept param, returns DispatchBoard shape: { columns: DispatchColumn[], jobs: DispatchJob[], wip_limits: Record<string, number> }; (b) dispatchQueueJob(jobId: string, targetColumn: string, assignedOperatorId?: string, assignedMachineId?: string) — calls POST /api/v1/erp/dispatch-queue-job with body; (c) dispatchReorder(columnId: string, jobIds: string[]) — calls POST /api/v1/erp/dispatch-reorder with { columnId, jobIds } for priority reordering within a column.

In KanbanBoardPage.tsx, replace INITIAL_COLUMNS with a static column definition (column IDs are fixed: 'queued', 'setup', 'running', 'inspection', 'complete', 'shipped') that drives the visual layout. Replace INITIAL_JOBS with a useEffect that calls getDispatchBoard() on mount and maps the returned jobs into their respective columns based on job.status. Add 30-second polling to refresh the board.

Replace HEIJUNKA_DATA with a derived leveling calculation: group jobs by due_date_hour and count jobs per hour bucket. Render as a small bar chart below the main board showing jobs-per-hour distribution for the current shift. Derive this from the live jobs array — no separate API call needed.

Wire drag-to-assign: when a card is dragged to a new column, call dispatchQueueJob(jobId, targetColumn). If the target column is 'running' or 'setup' and no machine is assigned, show a modal asking the manager to assign a machine and optionally an operator before confirming the move. On API success, update local state. On failure, revert the drag visually and show an error toast.

Add priority color coding to job cards: if job.priority === 'rush', render the card with a red left border and 'RUSH' badge; if 'normal', blue left border; if 'low', gray left border. All three priority levels must use both color AND a text label (not color alone) for color-blind accessibility.

Enforce WIP limits visually: if a column's job count meets or exceeds wip_limits[columnId], display the column header in orange with a warning icon 'WIP LIMIT REACHED'. Block drag-drops into over-limit columns and show a toast 'Column at WIP limit. Complete or move existing jobs first.'

Add GET /api/v1/erp/dispatch-board, POST /api/v1/erp/dispatch-queue-job, and POST /api/v1/erp/dispatch-reorder routes to src/routes/erp.ts. dispatch-board: query JobLifecycleEngine.listJobs() filtered to active/queued statuses, then query MachineDispatchEngine queue to annotate each job with machine and operator assignments. dispatch-queue-job: call MachineDispatchEngine.queueJob(jobId, machine, operator) and update job status via JobLifecycleEngine. dispatch-reorder: update queue_position for each job in the column. All three routes require verifyToken and requireRole('lead').
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors. Verify no references to INITIAL_COLUMNS, INITIAL_JOBS, or HEIJUNKA_DATA remain in KanbanBoardPage.tsx.

deliverables.description: All three seed arrays replaced. Board loads from /api/v1/erp/dispatch-board with 30s polling. Drag-to-assign calls dispatchQueueJob. Priority colors with text labels. WIP limit enforcement with blocking toast. Heijunka derived from live job due dates.
getDispatchBoard(), dispatchQueueJob(), dispatchReorder() API methods added.
GET /api/v1/erp/dispatch-board, POST /api/v1/erp/dispatch-queue-job, POST /api/v1/erp/dispatch-reorder routes added with lead role auth.

exit_conditions: No references to INITIAL_COLUMNS, INITIAL_JOBS, or HEIJUNKA_DATA remain in KanbanBoardPage.tsx
Board shows real jobs from MachineDispatchEngine queue across six columns (Queued/Setup/Running/Inspection/Complete/Shipped)
Drag-to-assign persists via API call and shows machine-assignment modal for running/setup columns
Priority uses both color AND text label — Rush=red+'RUSH', Normal=blue, Low=gray
WIP limit reached state blocks drag-drop and shows warning on column header
Heijunka view shows jobs-per-hour distribution derived from live job due dates
Board auto-refreshes every 30 seconds without user interaction
All three routes require lead clearance — shop_floor token returns 403
npm run build:fast passes with 0 errors

units.title: Wire RootCausePage to real scrap data and TroubleshootingEngine

steps.instruction: Read web/src/pages/RootCausePage.tsx in full (688 lines). Identify every reference to SEED_ANALYSES, SEED_FISHBONE_CAUSES, and SEED_ACTIONS. Note how the 5 Whys drill-down and Fishbone diagram are structured before proceeding.

Add two API functions to web/src/api/client.ts: (a) getRootCauseList(params?: { status?: string; dateFrom?: string; dateTo?: string }) — calls GET /api/v1/erp/root-cause-list, returns RootCauseAnalysis[]; (b) createRootCause(input: { job_number: string; job_time_entry_id: number; scrap_count: number; scrap_reason: string; initiated_by: string }) — calls POST /api/v1/erp/root-cause-create, returns the created RootCauseAnalysis.

In RootCausePage.tsx, replace SEED_ANALYSES with a useEffect that calls getRootCauseList() on mount. Display a loading spinner while fetching and an error banner on failure. Add an 'Incidents Needing Investigation' panel at the top: query job_time_entries where scrap_count > 0 and no root_cause_analysis_id exists, display as alert cards with a 'Investigate Root Cause' button that calls createRootCause() and navigates to the new analysis detail.

Replace SEED_FISHBONE_CAUSES with auto-generation: when viewing an analysis, call TroubleshootingEngine via POST /api/v1/erp/troubleshoot-diagnose with { symptom: scrap_reason, context: { job_number, machine_id, material, operation } }. Map the returned diagnosis to the six Fishbone categories — Man, Machine, Material, Method, Measurement, Environment — using the category field from each diagnostic finding. Populate the Fishbone diagram arms from this mapping.

Replace SEED_ACTIONS with real corrective actions stored in a root_cause_actions table. Wire the 'Add Action' form to call POST /api/v1/erp/root-cause-action-create with { analysis_id, description, assignee_id, due_date, category }. Wire the action status toggle to PATCH /api/v1/erp/root-cause-action-status with { action_id, status: 'open' | 'in_progress' | 'complete' }.

Auto-link to Kaizen: when a corrective action is marked 'complete', automatically create a Kaizen suggestion by calling POST /api/v1/erp/kaizen-status with { analysis_id, corrective_action_id, source: 'root_cause' }. Show a toast 'Action linked to Kaizen board.' Link the analysis card to any associated Kaizen suggestion.

Add GET /api/v1/erp/root-cause-list and POST /api/v1/erp/root-cause-create routes to src/routes/erp.ts. root-cause-list: SELECT from root_cause_analyses table with optional status and date filters. root-cause-create: INSERT into root_cause_analyses. Also add POST /api/v1/erp/troubleshoot-diagnose route that calls TroubleshootingEngine.diagnose(symptom, context) and returns findings. Add POST /api/v1/erp/root-cause-action-create and PATCH /api/v1/erp/root-cause-action-status routes. All routes require verifyToken.

Create migration src/db/migrations/015-root-cause-analyses.sql: CREATE TABLE root_cause_analyses (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, job_number VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, job_time_entry_id INTEGER REFERENCES job_time_entries(id), scrap_count INTEGER NOT NULL, scrap_reason TEXT NOT NULL, initiated_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open', 'in_progress', 'resolved', 'closed')), five_whys JSONB DEFAULT '[]', fishbone_causes JSONB DEFAULT '{}', created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()); CREATE TABLE root_cause_actions (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, analysis_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES root_cause_analyses(id), description TEXT NOT NULL, assignee_id VARCHAR(50), due_date DATE, category VARCHAR(50), status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' CHECK (status IN ('open', 'in_progress', 'complete')), kaizen_suggestion_id INTEGER REFERENCES kaizen_suggestions(id), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()); CREATE INDEX idx_rca_job ON root_cause_analyses(job_number); CREATE INDEX idx_rca_status ON root_cause_analyses(status);
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors. Verify no references to SEED_ANALYSES, SEED_FISHBONE_CAUSES, or SEED_ACTIONS remain in RootCausePage.tsx.

deliverables.description: All three seed arrays replaced. Incidents panel shows unanalyzed scrap entries with Investigate button. Fishbone auto-generated from TroubleshootingEngine.diagnose() mapped to 6M categories. Actions stored and loaded from DB. Completed actions auto-link to Kaizen board.
getRootCauseList(), createRootCause() API methods added.
GET /api/v1/erp/root-cause-list, POST /api/v1/erp/root-cause-create, POST /api/v1/erp/troubleshoot-diagnose, POST/PATCH root-cause-action routes added.
root_cause_analyses and root_cause_actions tables with FK to job_time_entries and kaizen_suggestions, status check constraints, indexes.

units.title: Wire A3ReportPage to real data and add PDF export

steps.instruction: Read web/src/pages/A3ReportPage.tsx in full (805 lines). Identify every reference to SEED_REPORTS and TEMPLATES. Note how the eight Toyota A3 sections are structured and what data each section expects before proceeding.

Add three API functions to web/src/api/client.ts: (a) getA3Reports(params?: { status?: string }) — calls GET /api/v1/erp/a3-report-list, returns A3Report[]; (b) createA3Report(input: { title: string; root_cause_analysis_id?: number; source_job_number?: string; created_by: string }) — calls POST /api/v1/erp/a3-report-create, returns A3Report; (c) getA3ReportPdf(reportId: string) — calls POST /api/v1/erp/a3-report-pdf/:id, returns a Blob for download.

In A3ReportPage.tsx, replace SEED_REPORTS with a useEffect that calls getA3Reports() on mount. Replace TEMPLATES with a static template list (keep the existing template names/structures — just remove the hardcoded seed data that represents pre-existing reports). Add a 'New A3 Report' button that opens a creation modal asking for title, linked root cause analysis (dropdown of open analyses), and source job number.

Wire auto-population for all 8 A3 sections: (1) Background — pull job.description, customer, part_number, order_quantity from JobLifecycleEngine via GET /api/v1/erp/job/:jobNumber; (2) Current Condition — pull current OEE for the relevant machine from analyticsOEE; (3) Goal — default to 'Reduce scrap rate to <1%, OEE >85%' with user-editable override; (4) Root Cause Analysis — pull five_whys JSONB from the linked root_cause_analyses record; (5) Countermeasures — pull root_cause_actions with status != 'complete' from the linked analysis; (6) Implementation Plan — auto-create from countermeasures with assignee + due_date fields; (7) Follow-up — show status of each action (open/in_progress/complete) as a checklist; (8) Results — pull scrap_rate before and after the analysis created_at date from job_time_entries aggregation.

Wire PDF export: add an 'Export PDF' button that calls getA3ReportPdf(reportId). The backend route should render the A3 report data into a structured PDF response using a template (use the existing pdf generation approach in the codebase — check src/engines/ and src/routes/ for any existing PDF generation pattern). The frontend should receive the Blob and trigger a browser download with filename `A3-${report.title}-${report.id}.pdf`.

Add GET /api/v1/erp/a3-report-list, POST /api/v1/erp/a3-report-create, GET /api/v1/erp/a3-report/:id, and POST /api/v1/erp/a3-report-pdf/:id routes to src/routes/erp.ts. All require verifyToken. a3-report-pdf: query the full A3 report with all 8 sections populated, generate PDF response with Content-Type: application/pdf header.

Create migration src/db/migrations/016-a3-reports.sql: CREATE TABLE a3_reports (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL, root_cause_analysis_id INTEGER REFERENCES root_cause_analyses(id), source_job_number VARCHAR(50), status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'in_review', 'approved', 'closed')), sections JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', created_by VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()); CREATE INDEX idx_a3_rca ON a3_reports(root_cause_analysis_id); CREATE INDEX idx_a3_status ON a3_reports(status);
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors. Verify no references to SEED_REPORTS remain in A3ReportPage.tsx.

phases.title: New Executive Dashboards & Display Modes
phases.description: Add three new production-grade pages: ExecutiveDashboardPage (P&L, revenue forecast, cash flow, customer rankings, headcount, on-time delivery), ShopFloorTVPage (wall-mount auto-rotating display, no auth), and DailyFlashReportEngine + DailyFlashReportPage (end-of-day auto-summary with email to management).

units.title: Create ExecutiveDashboardPage with financial and operational KPIs

steps.instruction: Create web/src/pages/ExecutiveDashboardPage.tsx. The page is protected at clearance_level='admin' via ProtectedRoute. Layout: a single-page KPI grid with six sections arranged in a 2-column responsive grid using Tailwind CSS. Use Recharts for all charts. Import and use the existing api/client functions for each data source.

Section 1 — P&L Summary: call getIncomeStatement(period: 'mtd' | 'ytd') — GET /api/v1/erp/income-statement?period=mtd. Display: Revenue, COGS, Gross Margin %, Operating Expenses, EBITDA, Net Income. Show MTD column and YTD column side by side. Add a green/red delta indicator vs prior period.

Section 2 — Revenue Forecast: call getRevenueForecast() — GET /api/v1/erp/revenue-forecast. Returns { pipeline_value, conversion_rate, forecast_30d, forecast_90d, backlog_value }. Derive: Forecast 30-day = pipeline_value * conversion_rate. Display as a KPI card with a Recharts BarChart showing current month actual vs forecast.

Section 3 — Cash Flow: call getCashFlow(period: 'mtd') — GET /api/v1/erp/cash-flow?period=mtd. Returns { cash_in, cash_out, net_cash_flow, ar_aging_0_30, ar_aging_31_60, ar_aging_over_60, ap_aging_0_30, ap_total }. Display: Net Cash Flow KPI, AR Aging donut chart (three age buckets using Recharts PieChart), AP Total.

Section 4 — Top 10 Customers by Revenue: call getTopCustomers(limit: 10, period: 'ytd') — GET /api/v1/erp/top-customers?limit=10&period=ytd. Returns Array<{ customer_name, ytd_revenue, ytd_margin_pct, job_count, last_order_date }>. Render as a table sorted descending by ytd_revenue with a small horizontal Recharts BarChart spark column.

units.title: Create ShopFloorTVPage (wall-mount auto-rotating display)

steps.instruction: Create web/src/pages/ShopFloorTVPage.tsx. The page must be readable at 15 feet: minimum font size 24px for body text, 48px for KPI values, 72px for primary headline numbers. Use a dark background (#111827) with high-contrast text (white, green, yellow, red). No interactive controls — read-only display.

Implement four auto-rotating panels using a setInterval that advances panel index every 8 seconds. Panel 1 — Machine Status Grid: show all active machines from getActiveMachineJobs() as large colored tiles (green=running, yellow=setup/paused, red=down/alarm, gray=idle). Each tile shows machine name and current operator name in 32px text. Panel 2 — OEE Today: show OEE % per machine as a large horizontal bar chart using Recharts, values in 48px font, color-coded green/yellow/red. Panel 3 — Job Queue: top 5 jobs by priority from getDispatchBoard(), each card showing job number (48px), part name, and time remaining. Panel 4 — Shift Countdown: current shift name (DAY/AFTERNOON/NIGHT), time remaining in shift as MM:SS countdown (72px), jobs completed this shift, and scrap rate today.

Wire real-time updates via WebSocket (same connection pattern as ShopFloorClockPage.tsx — read that file to understand the existing WebSocket client setup). On WebSocket message, update the relevant panel data without resetting the rotation timer. Fall back to 15-second polling if WebSocket is unavailable.

Add panel indicator dots at the bottom center: four dots, the current panel dot is white/filled, others are gray/hollow. No click needed — display only. Add a small 'PRISM Live' watermark in the bottom-right corner in 14px gray text.

Register the route in App.tsx: add <Route path='/app/shop-tv' element={<ShopFloorTVPage />} /> — NO ProtectedRoute wrapper, no auth required. Add 'Shop TV' entry to shellCatalog.ts with minClearance='none' so it appears in the sidebar for all users including unauthenticated ones.

Ensure the TV page calls only non-sensitive endpoints. It must NOT call any endpoint that returns employee pay rates, personal data, financial data, or customer names. Allowed endpoints: getActiveMachineJobs(), analyticsOEE (today only), getDispatchBoard() with a shop-tv-safe variant that omits operator personal data, and a new GET /api/v1/erp/shift-countdown (no auth) returning { shift_name, time_remaining_sec, jobs_completed_today, scrap_rate_today }.

Add GET /api/v1/erp/shift-countdown route to src/routes/erp.ts — this is one of the few routes that does NOT require verifyToken. Compute: current shift based on server time (day=06:00-14:00, afternoon=14:00-22:00, night=22:00-06:00), time_remaining_sec, count of job_time_entries with stop_time within today's shift, and scrap_rate_today from job_time_entries.
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors.

units.title: Create DailyFlashReportEngine and DailyFlashReportPage

steps.instruction: Create src/engines/DailyFlashReportEngine.ts. Export a singleton dailyFlashReportEngine. Implement generateFlashReport(date: string, requestedBy: string): Promise<DailyFlashReport>. The DailyFlashReport type: { date, generated_at, generated_by, jobs_completed: JobSummary[], jobs_in_progress: JobSummary[], scrap_rate_pct, good_parts_today, scrap_count_today, oee_by_machine: Array<{ machine_id, machine_name, oee_pct, availability_pct, performance_pct, quality_pct }>, labor_utilization_pct, productive_hours, shift_hours, on_time_delivery_pct, jobs_due_today, jobs_shipped_on_time, top_downtime_causes: Array<{ reason_category, total_minutes, count }> }. Pull data from TimeClockEngine, OEECalculatorEngine, JobLifecycleEngine, and MachineDispatchEngine. top_downtime_causes: aggregate pause_periods by reason_category for today's date, sort descending, take top 3.

Add daily_flash_generate action to businessDispatcher.ts: add 'daily_flash_generate' to the z.enum action list. Add a case handler calling dailyFlashReportEngine.generateFlashReport(params.date, params.requestedBy). Import from '../engines/DailyFlashReportEngine.js'. The action schema in businessActionSchemas.ts: daily_flash_generate requires { date: z.string() (ISO date), requestedBy: z.string() }. Both fields required, no .passthrough().

Add email dispatch to DailyFlashReportEngine: implement emailFlashReport(report: DailyFlashReport, recipients: string[]): Promise<void>. Use NotificationEngine (check src/engines/ for NotificationEngine.ts or EmailEngine.ts — use whatever notification engine exists). Format the email body as a plain-text summary with all KPIs. Subject line: `Daily Flash Report — ${report.date} — OEE: ${report.oee_avg_pct}% | Scrap: ${report.scrap_rate_pct}%`. If no notification engine exists, log a warning and resolve without throwing.

Add GET /api/v1/erp/flash-report and POST /api/v1/erp/flash-report-email routes to src/routes/erp.ts. flash-report: accepts query param ?date=YYYY-MM-DD (default today), calls dailyFlashReportEngine.generateFlashReport(date, req.user.id), returns the full report. flash-report-email: accepts { date, recipients: string[] }, generates and emails the report, returns { sent: true, recipient_count: number }. Both require verifyToken and requireRole('admin').

Create web/src/pages/DailyFlashReportPage.tsx. Layout: a date picker at the top (default today), a 'Generate Report' button, and the rendered report below. Report sections: (1) Header — date, generated_at, OEE average badge, scrap rate badge; (2) Jobs Today — two columns: Completed (list with part name, quantity, job number) and In Progress (list with % complete estimate); (3) Quality KPIs — good_parts_today, scrap_count_today, scrap_rate_pct as large colored tiles; (4) OEE by Machine — table with machine name, OEE%, Availability%, Performance%, Quality% color-coded; (5) Labor Utilization — productive_hours / shift_hours with a percentage bar; (6) On-Time Delivery — jobs_shipped_on_time / jobs_due_today as a percentage with green/yellow/red badge; (7) Top 3 Downtime Causes — ranked list with reason_category, count, total_minutes.

Add an 'Email to Management' button on DailyFlashReportPage. The button opens a small modal with a recipients list (pre-populated from localStorage key 'flash_report_recipients', editable). On confirm, call POST /api/v1/erp/flash-report-email. Show a success toast 'Report emailed to {n} recipients.'
Add getFlashReport(date?: string) and emailFlashReport(date: string, recipients: string[]) to web/src/api/client.ts.

Register the route in App.tsx: add <Route path='/app/flash-report' element={<ProtectedRoute minClearance='admin'><DailyFlashReportPage /></ProtectedRoute>} />. Add 'Daily Flash Report' to shellCatalog.ts with minClearance='admin'.
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors. Run npx tsc --noEmit to verify type safety of DailyFlashReportEngine.ts.

phases.title: OEE Dashboard Enhancement — Six Big Losses + Drill-Down
phases.description: Enhance the already-wired OEEDashboardPage (571 lines) with Six Big Losses breakdown, 30-day rolling OEE trend per machine using Recharts LineChart, machine drill-down modal with OEE components and top-5 downtime Pareto, and color-coded threshold system (Green >85%, Yellow 60-85%, Red <60%) with world-class target line.

units.title: Enhance OEEDashboardPage with Six Big Losses, trends, and drill-down

steps.instruction: Read web/src/pages/OEEDashboardPage.tsx in full (571 lines). Identify: (a) the exact API calls currently made (analyticsOEE, whoClockedIn); (b) how machines are listed; (c) the current chart components present. Note the existing color scheme and Recharts version before proceeding.

Add Six Big Losses breakdown section below the existing OEE summary. The six losses map to OEE components: Breakdowns (Availability loss — unplanned), Setup/Adjustment (Availability loss — planned), Minor Stops (Performance loss — short stoppages), Reduced Speed (Performance loss — speed loss), Startup Rejects (Quality loss — startup), Production Rejects (Quality loss — running). Add getOEESixLosses(machineId: string, date: string) to web/src/api/client.ts — calls GET /api/v1/erp/oee-six-losses?machineId=X&date=Y. Returns Array<{ loss_type: string, minutes_lost: number, pct_of_planned_time: number }>. Render as a Recharts BarChart sorted descending by minutes_lost.

Add 30-day rolling OEE trend per machine: add getOEETrend(machineId: string, days: 30) to web/src/api/client.ts — calls GET /api/v1/erp/oee-trend?machineId=X&days=30. Returns Array<{ date: string, oee_pct: number, availability_pct: number, performance_pct: number, quality_pct: number }>. Render as a Recharts LineChart with four lines (OEE, Availability, Performance, Quality) inside a ResponsiveContainer. Each machine card on the dashboard gets a small 'Trend' sparkline below its OEE value showing only the OEE line for the last 7 days.

Add machine drill-down: make each machine card clickable. On click, open a modal (Dialog component or custom overlay) for the selected machine. The drill-down modal contains three tabs: (a) Components — show Availability %, Performance %, Quality % as three large gauge or progress bar displays; (b) 30-Day Trend — the full 30-day LineChart for the selected machine; (c) Top 5 Downtime Pareto — Recharts ComposedChart (bars for minutes, cumulative % line) of the top 5 pause reason_categories for this machine in the last 30 days. Close the modal with ESC key or an X button.

Apply color-coded thresholds throughout the page: OEE value renders green if >85%, yellow if 60-85%, red if <60%. Apply to: OEE summary tile, each machine card header, trend chart reference lines, Six Big Losses bar colors. Add a world-class target line at 85% on the trend chart as a dashed Recharts ReferenceLine. Add a shop target line (configurable via localStorage key 'oee_shop_target', default 75%) as a second dashed line in a different color.

Add GET /api/v1/erp/oee-six-losses and GET /api/v1/erp/oee-trend routes to src/routes/erp.ts. oee-six-losses: compute each of the six loss categories from OEECalculatorEngine data and pause_periods table for the given machine and date. Map pause reason_categories to the six loss types: breakdown → Breakdowns, setup → Setup/Adjustment, minor_stop → Minor Stops, speed_loss → Reduced Speed. Startup and production rejects come from job_time_entries scrap_count split by process_type (setup vs production). Return all six losses sorted descending by minutes_lost. oee-trend: query aggregated OEE history per machine for the requested number of days. Both require verifyToken.
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors. Verify all Recharts components are wrapped in ResponsiveContainer to prevent crash on window resize.

hook.name: biz-ms3-no-seed-data-guard
hook.description: After any edit to a Lean dashboard page, grep the file for SEED_, INITIAL_, MOCK_, fixture patterns. If found, block commit with message: 'Lean page still contains hardcoded seed data — wire to real API before committing (BIZ-MS3 requirement).'

mcp_action.description: Generate end-of-day flash report aggregating jobs completed, scrap rate, OEE by machine, labor utilization, on-time delivery %, and top 3 downtime causes for a given date. Wires to DailyFlashReportEngine.generateFlashReport(date, requestedBy).

skill_enhancement.enhancement: Lean wiring patterns: replace seed arrays with useEffect API calls + loading/error states; derive secondary data (contributors, waste categories, heijunka) from the primary API response rather than separate calls; Recharts best practices (ResponsiveContainer mandatory, ComposedChart for Pareto bars+line, ReferenceLine for target values); Six Big Losses mapping to OEE components (Breakdowns+Setup=Availability, MinorStops+ReducedSpeed=Performance, StartupRejects+ProductionRejects=Quality split by process_type); WIP limit enforcement at both frontend (drag block) and backend (409 response); TV display accessibility (24px minimum body, 48px KPIs, 72px headlines, color+text labels not color alone).
